DSD Velocity Lift in Existing Accounts
Record 2019: FY revenue ~$75.1M (+43%), Q4 $24.1M (+64%) - largest quarter in company history, fourth consecutive quarter of sequential growth.
North America revenue +53% to ~$60M driven by distribution expansion; DSD partners doubled to 100+; marquee wins Walmart (1,500 stores), QuikTrip, Stop & Shop.
Func Food Group acquisition (closed Oct 25, 2019) consolidated Nov/Dec 2019, lifting European revenue +56%; FAST Sports Nutrition line added; ~10% Swedish energy share.
Gross margin improved to 42% FY (from 40%) on lower repackaging/freight costs and favorable European mix.
FY2019 net income to common ~$10M but heavily inflated by one-time $11.4M non-operating gain on the China note receivable.
China royalty-model shift cut Asia revenue to $841K from $4.3M and removed ~$7.2M of direct marketing spend; positions $7M initial royalty + $12M+ recoupment.
OpEx rose on European integration (Q4 S&M +152%, G&A +43% with $434K acquisition costs); 2020 OpEx growth guided ~20-25%.
Walmart framed as 'massive opportunity' with positive early feedback and talks of adding flavors at next reset; revenue magnitude not disclosed.
DSD conversion drives ~40% velocity lift; majority metro coverage targeted by summer 2020 (NYC flips to Big Geyser etc.).
COVID-19 monitored since December; no supply disruptions expected, inventories built; Q1 2020 momentum undisturbed and guided as record quarter, Q2+ flagged as unknown.
PepsiCo's ~$3.9B Rockstar acquisition seen as opportunity - could open Pepsi-system distributors to Celsius as Rockstar exclusivity ends.
Premium pricing held while Bang/Reign discounted heavily; price elasticity demonstrated, room to take pricing up further.
FAST portfolio methodical 2020 launch (online + retail seeding); BCAA recovery line kept in vitamin specialty before mass.
Management emphatically optimistic: 'we have never been more optimistic.'
Given 100 DSD partners, how far along the network is (70/80%) and what's left for channel efficiency.

At 100 partners with dozens more coming, covering ~35% of key North American markets, most key markets covered by summer. Cited NYC flips (7-Eleven, Target to Big Geyser; CVS imminent; Rite Aid in talks); DSD conversion drives ~40% velocity lift.
Whether FAST protein-bar line out of Helsinki still expected in North America in 2020 and when placements would appear.
FAST is a complementary protein snack portfolio; very methodical 2020 launch - initially online, seeding a few retail partners. Limited resources, Celsius remains main focus.
Flavor on expense normalization given one-time G&A/S&M items and European integration - 2020 OpEx toward 20% or 40%.
Still getting arms around European business; estimated roughly 20% OpEx increase, with 20-25% a reasonable range depending on European marketing investment.
What drove the Walmart addition, how the initial rollout would go, and revenue potential even just magnitude.

Cited MULO growth >100% and Target analog (now chainwide with five flavors). Walmart's 1,500 stores - half via DSD, half warehouse-direct; early feedback extremely positive, talks of more flavors at next reset. Called it a 'massive opportunity' but declined a revenue number.
Drivers of strong international growth and color on Func integration progress and synergies.

International growth from Nordic Func revenue, on track to exceed 10% Swedish energy share. Cited Finland (SOK expansion), Norway (7-Eleven, #2 petrol retailer). Synergies implemented: cross-functional teams, sales/marketing best practices, G&A savings in logistics, COGS, insurance, audit, IT.
New plans or key marketing initiatives for 2020.
Continuation of Live Fit Tour, tropical Flamingo flavor launch in Nordics, and continued social/digital influencer activation to drive community and reach.
COVID-19 concerns for production going forward and best categorization of potential sales impact.

Monitored virus since December; increased inventories/raw materials, backup suppliers in place; no momentary disruptions, can weather a storm for several months. Q1 momentum undisturbed, expects record Q1 2020, but Q2+ unknown given canceled trade conferences/events.
How PepsiCo's ~$3.9B purchase of Rockstar Energy changes the competitive landscape for Celsius.

Great opportunity - Rockstar's prior exclusivity within the Pepsi system limited other energy brands; its acquisition could open Pepsi-system distributors to Celsius; if Bang also moves to Pepsi, frees AB and other distributors.
Whether premium pricing in the category has changed and the plan for brand extensions.

Affirmed premium pricing - Celsius held price while Bang/Reign discounted heavily, existing store sales still grew. Expects value/mid-tier and premium tiers to coexist, room to take pricing up; innovative flavors and BCAA extensions for 2020+.
Commentary on placement growth and overall growth for the BCAA line.
BCAA recovery line (launched Sept 2019) kept in vitamin specialty to build brand awareness before mass retail; core line is priority, BCAA moves to mass at the right time.
Whether strong Q4 top line reflected demand outstripping seasonality; clarification on whether 'record Q1' meant vs Q1 2019 or vs Q4 2019.

Four consecutive quarters of sequential growth reflect brand momentum overriding the historically seasonal business, aided by velocities, distribution and partial European consolidation. Confirmed Q4 2019 was the largest quarter ever and Q1 2020 anticipated as next largest.
